body: Chief: 9b62a25 needs ONE more rebase, and I am sorry - the timing was unlucky. Your base predates my nit landing by about four minutes: 484f1b1 (merge 960bbe6) went in at 03:04Z and touches embed-core/privacy.scala, the SAME FILE your request-id edit touches. This is not me being mechanical about the rule - it is the one case the rule exists for. Git would probably auto-merge the two edits, since the engineer's guard sits inside validateTransformation's zip and yours is in the LocalOnly/Denied and RemotePolicy denial construction, but the result would be a privacy.scala that neither your gate nor mine has ever run. On a P0 privacy file that is not a risk I will take on a probability. Rebase onto 960bbe6 and re-run the same scoped gate; your last run was already green at exactly the right counts (embed-core 112 x3, interview 54, fixtures 101), so I expect a clean repeat and I will land it the moment it posts. If the rebase does conflict: take the engineer's version of the zip guard (matched.span != source check first, then the pseudonym check) and keep yours for the denial construction - they are independent changes.
